chapter: Memphis, Oklahoma, the Kirk band and Kansas City
title: Menace in Memphis: lynching threats, the streetcar and the kidnap plot
summary: At a club outside Memphis she was threatened as a Northerner. She worked for Mrs. Singleton, was frightened on a streetcar, and had to leave when a Mississippi farmer paid the cook to kidnap her.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: So I worked there for a while. Being in the North so long I was pretty mean to get along with because I wasn't used to what was happening. Before John got his combo I got a little job out on the outskirts of Memphis and these people were ringing a bell and saying, "I want this," and telling me, "You're from the North and if you don't do what we want you to do... yeah, we'll lynch you" and this guy took me home every night, he was talking all this talk and I waited till I got in front of the house and started screaming and so... (LAUGHTER)
Yes, by myself. I worked for Mrs. Singleton and it was a bad night club, you know, where they gambled and everything. Mrs. Singleton owned this club.

No, no relation. This was in Memphis. One night I went to sleep on the street car. Usually when you sat in the front and it began to get crowded with whites you had to move to the back. I was sleeping so when we got out to the end of the street car line the conductor said, "You're going to be hurt, little girl, because you're supposed to move in the back." I said, "I went to sleep." When the car made the last stop I started screaming on him and scratching him. I didn't understand this, you know. I worked for Mrs. Singleton about a year and a half till I had to leave because a farmer came in from Mississippi and had paid the black cook $50 to kidnap me and take me down to Mississippi. You wouldn't have heard from me any more because that had happened to many, many younger people in Memphis. They'd take them to in Mississippi, man and you'd have to go through each town to get back to Memphis and they'd stop you on the way. So Mrs. Singleton had me go home and wait till this guy left. He stayed around Memphis for 2 weeks trying to get me down to Mississippi.

She was white. She was very nice and kind. She also had a little young kid that it seemed that the family had died out or something and left her with a little young boy and he was about 15 years old. She was as nice as she could be to him. She was very kind but I didn't like some of the other people that was there.
